skill.name: fixing-accessibility
skill.description: Review UI work for accessibility issues and guide targeted fixes for names, keyboard access, focus, semantics, forms, contrast, and media.
skill.summary: Apply practical accessibility rules to UI reviews and fixes.
skill.author: ibelick

content.value_statement: Accessibility defects make interfaces harder to use and can block users from key workflows. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code clear rules for focused UI accessibility fixes.
actual_capabilities: Applies accessibility constraints to UI work in the current conversation.
Reviews a specified file against accessibility rules.
Reports violations with exact lines or snippets when available.
Explains why each accessibility issue matters in one short sentence.
Suggests targeted code-level fixes instead of broad rewrites.
Prioritizes accessible names, keyboard access, focus behavior, semantics, and forms.
limitations: It is guidance for AI-assisted review, not a full automated accessibility scanner.
It depends on the code and UI context provided in the conversation.
It does not replace manual testing with assistive technologies.
It avoids large rewrites unless the user requests broader refactoring.

use_cases.title: Review a New Component
use_cases.description: Check a new button, form, modal, or menu for missing labels, keyboard support, and focus behavior.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Pull Request
use_cases.description: Find accessibility issues before review and get small fixes that fit the existing implementation.

use_cases.title: Improve Design Handoff
use_cases.description: Translate accessibility expectations into concrete UI requirements for names, states, errors, and motion.

prompt_templates.title: Apply Accessibility Rules
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review for current UI work
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply the fixing-accessibility guidelines to my current UI changes. List the most important issues and suggest minimal fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Review One File
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this file with the fixing-accessibility skill. Quote each issue, explain why it matters, and suggest a targeted fix.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Component Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this component flow for accessible names, keyboard access, focus management, form errors, announcements, and contrast issues.

prompt_templates.title: Prioritize Complex Fixes
prompt_templates.prompt: Triage these accessibility findings by user impact. Propose the smallest safe changes and identify anything that needs manual assistive technology testing.

output: Issue: The button needs an accessible name.
Why it matters: Screen reader users need the control purpose.
Fix: Add a clear label that describes the delete action.
Issue: Focus should move into the dialog when it opens.
Why it matters: Keyboard users need a predictable starting point.
Fix: Set initial focus inside the dialog and restore focus on close.
Issue: The error text is not associated with the field.
Why it matters: Assistive technology may not announce the error.
Fix: Link the field to the error message and mark invalid fields clearly.

best_practices: Fix critical issues first, especially names, keyboard access, focus, and dialogs.
Prefer native HTML elements before adding ARIA roles or attributes.
Keep fixes small and aligned with the existing UI library.
anti_patterns: Do not add ARIA when native semantics already solve the problem.
Do not remove visible focus outlines without an accessible replacement.
Do not rely only on hover, color, or toast messages for important information.

faq.question: Does this skill run an automated accessibility test?
faq.answer: No. It provides review guidance and targeted fixes based on the code and UI context you provide.

faq.question: Can it review a single file?
faq.answer: Yes. Use it with a file and ask for violations, impact, and concrete fixes.

faq.question: Does it cover keyboard accessibility?
faq.answer: Yes. It checks Tab access, visible focus, Escape behavior, and keyboard support for custom controls.

faq.question: Does it support form accessibility?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers labels, required fields, error associations, aria-invalid, helper text, and disabled submit states.

faq.question: Should it replace a formal WCAG audit?
faq.answer: No. Use it for practical code review, then validate important flows with manual and automated testing.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
